title: The Milky Way above the ExTrA telescopes
caption: The Milky Way above the ExTrA telescopes, La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The Milky Way spreads across the sky above the three telescopes of the ExTrA project at ESO's La Silla Observatory. ESO Photo Ambassador Petr Horálek made this immersive view.
ExTrA searches for exoplanets, planets orbiting other stars, around a particular kind of star: red dwarfs. These stars are smaller, redder and cooler than our Sun.

That makes them good hunting grounds. Because the stars are small and dim, an Earth-sized planet makes a relatively bigger impression on its host, so such planets are easier to detect. Red dwarfs are also common. About 70% of stars in our part of the galaxy are red dwarfs, which makes them the most common places for exoplanets to exist. ESO describes them as the most common sites for exoplanets to exist, simply because there are so many of them.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at La Silla. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure collects more light than the eye can, so the Milky Way appears brighter and more detailed than it would to a visitor.

explore: ExTrA uses three telescopes for its search, all sited at La Silla. Because red dwarfs are cooler and redder than the Sun, they are a good match for a project built around finding Earth-sized worlds.
